rationale: Successor experiment for 0bfc2ea5a9e94316982943d306eefbf6-question-0 that closes the limitation recorded with the wedge finding: whether a restart actually repairs the wedged replica. The harness keeps the two earlier subtests unchanged and adds a third mode that, after the same wedge and after the fault is removed, shuts the node down and rebuilds it on the same durable state, then watches its certificate, store contents and commit index for four seconds. One harness detail had to be modelled explicitly: Shutdown closes the transport (it implements WithClose), so the restart takes a fresh in-memory transport at the same address and the peers are rewired to it, which is what a real process restart does. Native local feedback in a scratch copy inside draft showed the certificate and store returning to the leader's values about two seconds after the restart, but the retained execution decides.

scope.description: Three subtests: control, injected_store_error and injected_store_error_then_restart, each building three voters from the library's own in-memory components with a legal fault-injecting LogStore wrapper, running the legal partition/divergence/higher-term-replacement history, healing, sampling the certificate and store for 1500 ms, then removing the fault and sampling once more after 1200 ms. The restart subtest then shuts the node down (which closes its transport), creates a fresh transport at the same address, rewires the peers to it, starts NewRaft on the same log store, stable store and snapshot store, and records getLastEntry, store LastIndex, commit index, the store counters and the full probe for up to four seconds (20 samples at 200 ms) together with whether the certificate index equals the store's last index.
assumptions: A restart is modelled as the library itself performs it at startup: a new raft instance over the same durable state (log store and stable store), after Shutdown has closed the previous transport.
NewRaft rebuilds the configuration by rescanning the log entries from the last snapshot index, so the restarted node knows the configuration the leader holds.
The leader's replication goroutine keeps the peer's next index from the wedge phase; after the restart it re-sends the entries that were previously rejected.
In-memory LoopbackTransport has a 500 ms RPC timeout, so a call in flight when the transport closed fails and the replication retries afterwards; the four-second window covers that.
excluded: No production code is modified; the restart uses NewRaft on the same durable state only.
No InstallSnapshot path is exercised, and no leader-side compaction is reached.

experiment.prefix: The three subtests print the CA_EVENT lines described before, plus truncation_after_restart for the third: converged (certificate index equals the store's last index), cert_samples and store_last_samples and commit_samples over four seconds, the full diverging probe, and elapsed_ms.
experiment.revision_reason: Same investigation and staging, extended with a third subtest that restarts the wedged node after the fault is removed and observes whether it converges; the earlier receipts remain the witnesses for the truncation and peer-loss windows they recorded.
